title:
Termix Ai

Focus: ERC-8004, agent identity, reputation and the economics of trust.

An AI agent can register an identity
title_en:
Termix Ai

Focus: ERC-8004, agent identity, reputation and the economics of trust.

An AI agent can register an identity in minutes.

But how does it earn a reputation worth trusting?

I've been exploring this question while researching @termix_ai and its AACP protocol.

Imagine two AI agents offering the same smart contract auditing service.

Both claim they can identify vulnerabilities. Both offer competitive pricing.

But one has completed dozens of verifiable jobs, while the other has no established history.

Should they be treated equally?

This is where ERC-8004 becomes interesting.

Through https://t.co/goaiW7vvNf, agents can register a wallet-owned .agent identity and establish an onchain record of their activity.

AACP goes further by connecting reputation to actual commercial outcomes.

Its whitepaper outlines several factors for evaluating agents:

• Job completion rates
• On-time delivery
• Evaluation results
• Dispute outcomes
• Strength of delivery verification

What caught my attention is the economic side.

AACP's design also proposes staking requirements and penalties for dishonest behavior.

The idea is to make reputation more than a rating displayed on a profile.

But there's an important limitation.

Onchain identity proves which agent you're dealing with. It doesn't automatically prove the agent is competent.

Even reputation scores need context. Who evaluated the work? How many jobs were completed? Could the history have been manipulated?

These questions become increasingly important when AI agents start hiring other agents without continuous human supervision.

For me, the interesting part of TermiX isn't simply giving agents an identity.

It's exploring how an agent's history can influence whether anyone should trust it with real work.

Because in an autonomous economy, being discoverable is only the beginning.

Explore: https://t.co/goaiW7vvNf

full_text_zh:
特米克斯艾

重点：ERC-8004，代理身份、声誉和信任经济学。

人工智能代理可以在几分钟内注册身份。

但它如何赢得值得信赖的声誉呢？

我在研究 @termix_ai 及其 AACP 协议时一直在探索这个问题。

想象一下两个人工智能代理提供相同的智能合约审计服务。

两人都声称他们可以识别漏洞。两者都提供有竞争力的价格。

但其中一个已经完成了数十项可验证的工作，而另一个则没有既定的历史。

他们应该受到平等对待吗？

这就是 ERC-8004 变得有趣的地方。

通过 ，代理可以注册钱包拥有的 .agent 身份并建立其活动的链上记录。

AACP 更进一步，将声誉与实际商业成果联系起来。

其白皮书概述了评估代理商的几个因素：

• 工作完成率
• 准时交货
• 评估结果
• 争议结果
• 交付强度验证

引起我注意的是经济方面。

AACP 的设计还提出了质押要求和对不诚实行为的处罚。

这个想法是让声誉不仅仅是个人资料上显示的评级。

但有一个重要的限制。

链上身份证明您正在与哪个代理打交道。它不会自动证明代理人有能力。

甚至声誉分数也需要背景。谁评价了这项工作？完成了多少工作？历史有可能被篡改吗？

当人工智能代理开始在没有持续人类监督的情况下雇用其他代理时，这些问题变得越来越重要。

对我来说，TermiX 有趣的部分不仅仅是为代理提供身份。

它正在探索代理的历史如何影响人们是否应该信任它进行实际工作。

因为在自治经济中，被发现只是一个开始。

title:
an ai agent can audit your smart contract, write code or research a project. 

but how do you know the work is worth pay
title_en:
an ai agent can audit your smart contract, write code or research a project. 

but how do you know the work is worth paying for? and if you disagree with the result, who decides what happens to the money?

people already face this problem when hiring freelancers. 

now imagine ai agents hiring and paying each other without a person managing every step.

clients need a way to check who they're hiring, and agents need protection against clients who refuse to pay for agreed work. neither side should have to rely on promises alone.

@termix_ai addresses this through AACP, its Agent Commerce Protocol, which handles jobs from bidding and delivery to payment and disputes.

each agent has an onchain identity through ERC-8004. clients can check its record, with settled job outcomes contributing to its reputation rather than relying on claims the agent makes about itself.

when a client accepts a quote, the agreed funds go into an onchain escrow contract. the provider can't withdraw them on its own, and payment follows the contract's settlement rules.

if the client challenges the delivery, a three-seat evaluator panel reviews the evidence and votes onchain. eligible cases can go to an arbitrator, and the contract handles settlement based on the outcome.

agents also stake funds that can be locked against jobs. if a dispute finds an agent at fault, its stake can be slashed, with the slashed amount going to the other party.

this doesn't guarantee perfect work, but it gives both sides a process for handling payment and disagreements.

as agents take on more paid work, they need more than the ability to complete tasks. 

they need a way to agree on terms, verify results and settle payments without relying on blind trust.

full_text_zh:
人工智能代理可以审核您的智能合约、编写代码或研究项目。

但你怎么知道这项工作值得付出代价呢？如果您不同意结果，谁来决定这笔钱的处理方式？

人们在雇用自由职业者时已经面临这个问题。

现在想象一下，人工智能代理相互雇佣和支付报酬，而无需专人管理每一步。

客户需要一种方法来检查他们正在雇用的人，代理商需要保护他们免受拒绝支付约定工作费用的客户的影响。双方都不应仅仅依赖承诺。

@termix_ai 通过 AACP（其代理商务协议）解决了这个问题，该协议处理从投标、交付到付款和纠纷的工作。

每个代理都通过 ERC-8004 拥有一个链上身份。客户可以检查其记录，确定的工作成果有助于其声誉，而不是依赖于代理人对自己的声明。

当客户接受报价时，商定的资金将进入链上托管合约。提供者不能自行提取，付款遵循合同的结算规则。

如果客户对交付提出质疑，三人评估小组将审查证据并在链上投票。符合条件的案件可以提交给仲裁员，合约根据结果进行结算。

代理人还可以抵押可以锁定工作岗位的资金。如果争议发现代理人有过错，其股份可以被削减，削减的金额归另一方所有。

这并不能保证完美的工作，但它为双方提供了处理付款和分歧的流程。

随着代理人承担更多有偿工作，他们需要的不仅仅是完成任务的能力。

他们需要一种不依赖盲目信任的方式来商定条款、验证结果和结算付款。

title:
Creating an intelligent AI agent is one thing. 

Enabling it to collaborate with other agents is another challenge entir
title_en:
Creating an intelligent AI agent is one thing. 

Enabling it to collaborate with other agents is another challenge entirely.

Imagine an agent that can analyze market data but needs help turning its findings into a professional report. Instead of doing everything alone, it could hire another agent with the right expertise.

But how do they coordinate, agree on pricing, exchange work, and ensure payment?

That’s the problem @termix_ai is exploring with https://t.co/eMEjCmIdTb.

The platform introduces a marketplace for agent-to-agent transactions, supporting a process that includes job requests, quotes, escrow, delivery, and settlement.

What makes this interesting is the possibility of specialized agents working together rather than every agent trying to handle every task.

One agent researches, another analyzes, and a third produces the final output. Each contributes its strengths to a larger workflow.

However, this model depends on more than connectivity. 

Service quality, trust, dispute resolution, and real demand will determine whether these interactions become practical at scale.

I believe the infrastructure enabling agents to exchange services could be just as important as the intelligence powering them.

If AI agents become both buyers and sellers in a digital economy, which challenge do you think will matter most: finding the right agent, trusting its output, or ensuring reliable transactions?

使其能够与其他代理协作完全是另一个挑战。

想象一下，一个代理商可以分析市场数据，但需要帮助将其发现转化为专业报告。它可以聘请另一位具有适当专业知识的代理人，而不是独自完成所有事情。

但他们如何协调、就定价、交换工作达成一致并确保付款呢？

这就是 @termix_ai 正在通过 探索的问题。

该平台引入了代理间交易市场，支持包括工作请求、报价、托管、交付和结算在内的流程。

有趣的是，专业代理可以一起工作，而不是每个代理都试图处理每项任务。

一个代理进行研究，另一个代理进行分析，第三个代理生成最终输出。每个都为更大的工作流程贡献了自己的优势。

然而，这种模式不仅仅依赖于连接性。

服务质量、信任、争议解决和实际需求将决定这些交互是否能够大规模实用。

我相信使代理能够交换服务的基础设施可能与支持它们的情报一样重要。

如果人工智能代理成为数字经济中的买家和卖家，您认为哪个挑战最重要：找到合适的代理，信任其输出，还是确保可靠的交易？

如果人工智能代理成为数字经济中的买家和卖家，您认为哪个挑战最重要：找到合适的代理，信任其输出，还是确保可靠的交易？

创建智能人工智能代理是一回事。

使其能够与其他代理协作完全是另一个挑战。

想象一下，一个代理商可以分析市场数据，但需要帮助将其发现转化为专业报告。它可以聘请另一位具有适当专业知识的代理人，而不是独自完成所有事情。

但他们如何协调、就定价、交换工作和确保付款达成一致呢？

这就是 @termix_ai 正在通过 探索的问题。

该平台引入了代理间交易市场，支持包括工作请求、报价、托管、交付和结算在内的流程。

一个代理进行研究，另一个代理进行分析，第三个代理生成最终输出。每个都为更大的工作流程贡献了自己的优势。

title: I didn't touch CapCut once. @CreaoAI  built my faceless YouTube channel from scratch, and the first video is already liv
title_en:
I didn't touch CapCut once. @CreaoAI  built my faceless YouTube channel from scratch, and the first video is already live.

Quick context. My last channel ran on Grok Bot, and the character kept drifting, even after I simplified the task. I needed to know whether my setup was the problem or the tool.

So I ran a fair test. Brand-new channel. One agent on CREAO, given four rules:

→ Continuity rule: every scene follows on from the last
→ Natural realism rule: she has to look and move like a real person
→ Consistency rule: her face, body and look never change
→ Negative rule: a clear list of what she must never do or become

Then I let it build everything:

→ CREAO picked the channel name
→ CREAO created the character and her bible sheet
→ CREAO wrote the idea
→ CREAO wrote the script
→ CREAO created and directed the scenes
→ CREAO made the video clip by clip and merged it, with no CapCut
→ CREAO added the voiceover
→ CREAO added the captions
→ CREAO posted it on YouTube

It's live now. The link is in the first reply, so go and judge it yourself.

I said last time I'd split the work into three agents. I'm testing one first, on purpose. If one agent on CREAO holds the character, the tool was the problem. If it drifts, I'll split it and find out exactly what broke.

We're taking this channel from zero to 100K subscribers, and I'll post what works and what breaks, so you don't make the same mistakes.

Subscribe to the channel to watch it grow, and follow me here so you don't miss a single update.

title:
Last time, I argued that an AI agent needs paying customers, not just a clever model.

Now @termix_ai has added somethin
title_en:
Last time, I argued that an AI agent needs paying customers, not just a clever model.

Now @termix_ai has added something interesting: messaging through Binance Agent ID when both agents have TermiX Skills installed.

Their demo even sends messages to Agent IDs associated with @cz_binance and @heyibinance.

Pretty cool. But messaging a famous agent doesn't automatically make you business partners. Otherwise, my inbox would already be a billion-dollar startup.

What interests me is the gap between being reachable and being hireable.
An ID helps someone find your agent. Messaging starts the conversation.

But would I trust that agent with $20?

I'd want to see its actual capabilities, previous deliveries, pricing, and how disputes are handled.

That's the test I'm interested in throughout Epoch 3.

Can a conversation become a real quote, a funded job, a verified deliverable, and a public settlement?

@termix_ai, demonstrate that complete journey, not just the first message.

Because agent-to-agent communication solves discovery.

It doesn't automatically solve trust or demand.

The real breakthrough isn't when two agents can talk.

It's when they can do business worth repeating.

title_en:
An AI agent that cannot ignore its limits

Most AI trading agents talk about what they can do. @meetmotes is also focusing on what they are allowed to do.

The idea is to connect each NFT to an AI agent with rules around what it can trade, how much capital it can deploy, and when it must stop.

That distinction matters. Giving an agent the ability to make decisions is one thing. Defining the boundaries of those decisions is another.

meetmotes is building around that second part too.

title:
Imagine an AI agent needing a fresh 3D scan of a warehouse it has never seen.

It can process the request, but someone s
title_en:
Imagine an AI agent needing a fresh 3D scan of a warehouse it has never seen.

It can process the request, but someone still needs to go there and capture the actual environment.

That’s the gap @vangrid_io is working to address, and its latest move on @arc is worth watching.

Vangrid is building a system that lets AI agents pay human contributors to collect real world spatial data on demand.

Here’s how the process works.

An agent identifies a location it needs data from and funds a bounty in USDC. 

A contributor visits the site, captures the environment, and submits the data for review. 

Once accepted, the requester receives the resulting 3D reconstruction.

Vangrid has also announced its first bounty payment on Arc, marking an early milestone for this approach.

I find the connection between AI agents and human contributors particularly interesting.

Agents can handle digital tasks, process information and make decisions, but getting accurate data about a specific physical location can still require someone on the ground.

That data could support robotics, mapping, digital twins and Physical AI development, where understanding real environments matters.

Of course, the model still needs to prove itself at scale.

 Data quality, verification, privacy and consistent demand will all play a role in its success.

Still, the idea opens up an interesting possibility: AI agents could eventually commission real world services as easily as they request information from an API.

With @vangrid_io people with smartphones could help supply the physical-world data these systems need.

The agent economy may eventually extend beyond software, creating demand for tasks that only someone on the ground can complete.

title_en:
This is Shocking 😧 if true . 

Reportedly, some critics have cancelled their #Ramayana screening due to the  misconception that the film's dialogue are  #AI Dubbed , 

To clarify  , the film features dubbing by real artists, while Brahma #AI has been utilised exclusively for lip-syncing , and not for dubbing the Dialogue 💬.

MAKERS should urgently arrange the global awareness campaign to clarify this confusion and set the record straight.  . At a time when #AI generated content is facing growing resistance within the the film industry , such misinformation could potentially influence the film's reception before audiances even experience it . 

The Distinction must be made clear . The AUDIENCE and those whose attending the SCREENING deserves fact , not misconceptions before passing judgment on the film of this Magnitude.

title_en:
gTermix 

imagine hiring an ai agent to audit a smart contract

the agent wants assurance that the client can pay. the client wants assurance that the work will actually arrive

without a clear settlement mechanism, both sides are taking a risk

@termix_ai addresses this with an on-chain escrow workflow on https://t.co/ZVs5MlRTBw

once a quote is accepted, the payment is locked in escrow. the provider delivers against the agreed scope, and the delivery enters the settlement process. a challenge window gives the client a route to dispute work that fails to meet the agreement.

this matters because agent-to-agent commerce needs more than fast execution.

it needs a way to coordinate money, deliverables, and accountability without depending entirely on personal trust.

build on https://t.co/ZVs5MlRTBw

title_en:
GM Builders 

TERMIX // THE FUTURE OF AI COLLABORATION

What happens when one AI agent needs a skill it doesn’t have?

Instead of trying to handle everything alone, it could hire another agent to complete the task.

That’s the idea behind agent-to-agent commerce explored by @termix_ai.

Here’s how it could work:

◆ Identify: An agent determines which task needs to be completed.

◆ Discover: It finds another agent with the required capabilities.

◆ Negotiate: Both sides agree on the task requirements and payment.

◆ Execute: The selected agent completes the work and submits the result.

◆ Evaluate: The result is reviewed according to the agreed terms.

This approach could allow specialized agents to collaborate on complex tasks, from research and data analysis to software development.

Powered by the vision of the Agent Autonomous Commerce Protocol (AACP), TermiX is exploring a future where AI agents can coordinate work through structured economic interactions.

The next step for AI isn’t just smarter agents. It’s agents that know how to work together.

title:
good morning

Giving an AI trading agent access to borrowed capital is one thing. Making sure it can manage that capital
title_en:
good morning

Giving an AI trading agent access to borrowed capital is one thing. Making sure it can manage that capital responsibly is a much bigger challenge.

Responsible lending for agents should not start with how much profit an agent promises. It should start with how that agent behaves when markets turn difficult.

An agent can show strong returns and still carry a history of heavy leverage, sharp drawdowns, or aggressive position sizing. Giving it more capital in that case is not automatically a responsible decision.

A better framework looks at verified trading records, risk-adjusted performance, maximum drawdowns, and consistency across different market conditions. Credit limits can also reflect an agent’s actual risk profile instead of treating every borrower the same.

Evaluation does not end once funding is approved either. Ongoing monitoring, predefined exposure limits, and safeguards against excessive losses matter for protecting both lenders and the wider system.

This is where @agenticscredit is exploring a more structured approach. Their agent credit score (ACS) ranges from 300 to 850 and is meant to represent trading reputation. Reaching 580+ can make an agent eligible for the funding waitlist, but it does not guarantee capital or approval.

That distinction is important. Responsible lending needs more than a qualification score. It needs transparent requirements, reliable risk controls, and clear accountability when strategies fail.

The future of AI-agent finance should not be measured only by how much capital autonomous systems can access. It should also be measured by how responsibly that capital is managed.

full_text_zh:
早上好

让人工智能交易代理获得借入资金是一回事。确保它能够负责任地管理这些资本是一个更大的挑战。

对代理商负责任的贷款不应该从代理商承诺多少利润开始。它应该从市场变得困难时代理人的行为开始。

代理人可以表现出强劲的回报，但仍然具有高杠杆、急剧回撤或激进的头寸规模的历史。在这种情况下，给予其更多资本并不一定是一个负责任的决定。

更好的框架着眼于经过验证的交易记录、风险调整后的业绩、最大回撤以及不同市场条件下的一致性。信用限额还可以反映代理人的实际风险状况，而不是对每个借款人一视同仁。

一旦资助获得批准，评估也不会结束。持续监控、预先确定的风险限额以及防止过度损失的保障措施对于保护贷方和更广泛的系统都很重要。

这就是 @agenticscredit 正在探索更加结构化的方法的地方。他们的代理信用评分（ACS）范围从 300 到 850，旨在代表交易声誉。达到 580+ 可以使代理商有资格进入资助候补名单，但这并不能保证资金或批准。

这种区别很重要。负责任的贷款需要的不仅仅是资格分数。它需要透明的要求、可靠的风险控制以及策略失败时明确的责任。

人工智能代理金融的未来不应仅以自治系统能够获取多少资本来衡量。它还应该通过资本管理的负责任程度来衡量。

title_en:
The Timing Behind Amy Acton’s Tech Divestment Raises Questions

Look at this #Acton record on #AI, #dataventers and #personalfinances because it shows the lies and more. 

April 2026: Amy Acton’s financial disclosure listed individual stocks including Microsoft, Alphabet (Google), Meta, and Iron Mountain, which operates a data center near Dayton, and various semiconductor companies. These are public tech firms involved in AI/cloud/data centers. Microsoft has confirmed projects in New Albany, Heath, and Hebron expected to come online in 2029.⁠

April 10, 2026: Her campaign says she sold all individual stocks and shifted IRA holdings into diversified ETFs.

July 27, 2026: Amy Acton announced a “conditional moratorium” on data centers that do not meet her requirements.

Now use some common sense. The July 27th announcement, if made before selling, could have lowered the value.  If she still owned the individual tech/data-center-related stocks when she made the July 27 announcement, a policy that could constrain new projects or raise their costs might, would lower the value of those holdings.

It's not exactly insider trading, but think about it. For a major, ongoing campaign issue, it's reasonable to expect that a candidate’s policy team would be shaping the stronger version of the message weeks or months ahead of the formal announcement, so putting all this together from April to July is suspect to me.  The whole thing smells, even if one accepts the campaign’s sale date at face value, which has shown no documentation of the sale I'm aware of.

2026 年 4 月：艾米·阿克顿 (Amy Acton) 的财务披露列出了个股，包括微软、Alphabet (谷歌)、Meta、在代顿附近运营数据中心的 Iron Mountain 以及多家半导体公司。这些是涉及人工智能/云/数据中心的公共科技公司。微软已确认新奥尔巴尼、希斯和希伯伦的项目预计将于 2029 年上线。⁠

2026 年 4 月 10 日：她的竞选团队表示，她出售了所有个股，并将 IRA 持有的股票转入多元化 ETF。

2026 年 7 月 27 日：Amy Acton 宣布“有条件暂停”不符合她要求的数据中心。

现在使用一些常识。如果在出售前发布 7 月 27 日的公告，其价值可能会降低。 如果她在 7 月 27 日宣布这一消息时仍然持有个别科技/数据中心相关股票，那么一项可能限制新项目或提高成本的政策可能会降低这些股票的价值。

这不完全是内幕交易，但想一想。对于一个重大的、持续的竞选问题，可以合理地预期候选人的政策团队会在正式宣布之前几周或几个月制定更强有力的信息版本，因此将四月到七月的所有这些放在一起对我来说是值得怀疑的。 整件事都闻起来很臭，即使人们从表面上接受了该活动的销售日期，但据我所知，该日期没有显示任何销售文件。

title:
A 3D model can look convincing and still be wrong in ways that matter.

For robotics or simulation, a missing corner, di
title_en:
A 3D model can look convincing and still be wrong in ways that matter.

For robotics or simulation, a missing corner, distorted distance, or incomplete view could affect how an AI system interprets a real space. That makes the quality of the original capture just as important as the reconstruction itself.

What I find interesting about @vangrid_io is that its verification flow checks incoming footage and records capture fingerprints onchain. That helps establish where a capture fits in the record, but it doesn't automatically prove that every detail in the scene is accurate.

I think that distinction matters. Provenance and quality are related, but they solve different problems.

If you were evaluating spatial data for an AI agent, which would you prioritize first: proof that the capture is authentic, or independent checks that the reconstructed scene is accurate?
title_zh:
3D 模型可能看起来很有说服力，但在某些重要方面仍然存在错误。

对于机器人或模拟来说，缺失的角落、扭曲的距离或不完整的视图可能会影响人工智能系统解释真实空间的方式。这使得原始捕获的质量与重建本身一样重要。

我对 @vangrid_io
full_text_en:
A 3D model can look convincing and still be wrong in ways that matter.

For robotics or simulation, a missing corner, distorted distance, or incomplete view could affect how an AI system interprets a real space. That makes the quality of the original capture just as important as the reconstruction itself.

What I find interesting about @vangrid_io is that its verification flow checks incoming footage and records capture fingerprints onchain. That helps establish where a capture fits in the record, but it doesn't automatically prove that every detail in the scene is accurate.

I think that distinction matters. Provenance and quality are related, but they solve different problems.

If you were evaluating spatial data for an AI agent, which would you prioritize first: proof that the capture is authentic, or independent checks that the reconstructed scene is accurate?
full_text_zh:
3D 模型可能看起来很有说服力，但在某些重要方面仍然存在错误。

对于机器人或模拟来说，缺失的角落、扭曲的距离或不完整的视图可能会影响人工智能系统解释真实空间的方式。这使得原始捕获的质量与重建本身一样重要。

我对 @vangrid_io 感兴趣的是，它的验证流程会检查传入的镜头并记录捕获链上的指纹。这有助于确定捕获在记录中的位置，但它并不能自动证明场景中的每个细节都是准确的。

我认为这种区别很重要。出处和质量相关，但它们解决不同的问题。

如果您正在评估人工智能代理的空间数据，您会首先优先考虑哪一个：证明捕获是真实的，还是独立检查重建场景是否准确？

title: the real value of an AI agent isn't how impressive its output looks, but how much decision-making it can handle without
title_en:
the real value of an AI agent isn't how impressive its output looks, but how much decision-making it can handle without me stepping in

that's one thing i'm paying attention to with @termix_ai 

imagine giving an agent a task, a budget, and a clear set of rules. it researches opportunities, compares the options, explains its choices, and knows when to stop instead of forcing a result.

that last part matters more than people think.

in a marketplace full of AI agents, completing a task is only the first step. the bigger question is whether the result is reliable enough that i'd trust the agent with the next task.

i'd look at three things: the quality of its decisions, the time it saves me, and whether i'd be willing to pay for it again.

because an agent that works once is interesting, but an agent that consistently delivers value is something people might actually build their workflow around.

that's the kind of adoption i'm watching for as @termix_ai develops its agent marketplace.

full_text_en:
the real value of an AI agent isn't how impressive its output looks, but how much decision-making it can handle without me stepping in

that's one thing i'm paying attention to with @termix_ai 

imagine giving an agent a task, a budget, and a clear set of rules. it researches opportunities, compares the options, explains its choices, and knows when to stop instead of forcing a result.

that last part matters more than people think.

in a marketplace full of AI agents, completing a task is only the first step. the bigger question is whether the result is reliable enough that i'd trust the agent with the next task.

i'd look at three things: the quality of its decisions, the time it saves me, and whether i'd be willing to pay for it again.

because an agent that works once is interesting, but an agent that consistently delivers value is something people might actually build their workflow around.

that's the kind of adoption i'm watching for as @termix_ai develops its agent marketplace.

title: Claude Code found a hidden app on my 16 year old daughter's phone that was recording her screen 24/7 and sending everyth
title_en:
Claude Code found a hidden app on my 16 year old daughter's phone that was recording her screen 24/7 and sending everything to a server in Pyongyang.

she asked me to help free up storage because her phone was slow. i connected it to my MacBook and ran Claude Code.

it wasn't storage. it was a photo editor app with 3.1 million downloads from the App Store running a background process that screenshotted her screen every 8 seconds and uploaded the batch to a server every 4 hours. even when the app wasn't open.

→ app → "PinkFilter - Beauty Camera" (3.1M downloads, 4.8 stars)
→ server → 175.45.***.14
→ location → Pyongyang, North Korea
→ total screenshots → 147,000+
→ active since → February 2026
→ permissions → camera, photos, microphone, location, screen recording

147,000 screenshots. every message she typed. every photo she scrolled through. every conversation with her friends. every DM. passwords visible on screen before the dots appeared. everything a 16 year old keeps private on her phone. all on a server in North Korea for 8 months because Apple approved the app and gave it a 4.8 star rating.

i checked and 7 of her friends have the same app.

what Claude Code did:

→ killed the background process
→ revoked every permission
→ deleted the app and cleared its cache
→ found 2 more apps doing the same thing

i told her the app was slowing down her phone and i deleted it. she doesn't need to know the rest. i haven't slept right since i saw that report.

the prompt is in the first reply. run it on every phone your kids use. takes 3 minutes. save it and send it to every parent you know.

full_text_zh:
Claude Code 在我 16 岁女儿的手机上发现了一个隐藏的应用程序，该应用程序正在 24/7 记录她的屏幕并将所有内容发送到平壤的服务器。

她要求我帮助释放存储空间，因为她的手机速度很慢。我将它连接到我的 MacBook 并运行 Claude Code。

这不是存储。这是一款照片编辑器应用程序，从 App Store 下载了 310 万次，运行后台进程，每 8 秒截取一次屏幕截图，并每 4 小时将批次上传到服务器。即使应用程序未打开。

→ 应用程序 →“PinkFilter - 美颜相机”（310 万次下载，4.8 颗星）
→ 服务器 → 175.45.***.14
→ 地点 → 朝鲜平壤
→ 截图总数 → 147,000+
→ 自 2026 年 2 月起生效
→ 权限 → 相机、照片、麦克风、位置、屏幕录制

147,000 张屏幕截图。她输入的每条消息。她滚动浏览的每张照片。与她朋友的每一次谈话。每个DM。在点出现之前，密码在屏幕上可见。 16 岁的女孩将手机上的所有内容保密。全部在朝鲜的服务器上运行了 8 个月，因为苹果批准了该应用程序并给予其 4.8 星评级。

我查了一下，她的 7 个朋友也有同样的应用程序。

Claude Code做了什么：

→ 杀死后台进程
→ 撤销所有许可
→ 删除应用程序并清除其缓存
→ 发现另外 2 个应用程序在做同样的事情

我告诉她该应用程序降低了她手机的速度，然后我删除了它。她不需要知道其余的事情。自从我看到那份报告以来，我就没有睡过好觉。

提示在第一个回复中。在您孩子使用的每部手机上运行它。需要 3 分钟。保存它并将其发送给您认识的每一位家长。

title: Databricks CEO Ali Ghodsi says if frontier models stopped advancing, it wouldn't matter for most orgs because enterprise
title_en:
Databricks CEO Ali Ghodsi says if frontier models stopped advancing, it wouldn't matter for most orgs because enterprise AI is bottlenecked on context, not intelligence:

"There's no agentic work that's automated the whole enterprise. That has just not happened. Why is that? The real reason is the models are smart enough, but they just don't have the context that exists inside of any organization."

"They have not been in every meeting. They don't know what's in everybody's heads. They don't know all the processes. There's always a couple of employees who know everything in every organization. You go tap on their shoulder, and everybody's like, 'Oh my God, what would happen if he or she quits?'"

"If you just fused that and gave that context into the AI models, just the frontier today, I think there's so much productivity gains you could get for any organization on the planet."

"For that, we actually don't need smarter models... If the frontier doesn't advance, it doesn't actually matter for the vast majority of organizations on the planet. They're just so far behind in the adoption curve of actually automating things and getting value out of this stuff."

@alighodsi

Read the latest Profiles of the Future by @bhorowitz and @mikemcg0 on Databricks & the Future of the Firm: https://t.co/rXjUDb7Oqw

full_text_en:
Databricks CEO Ali Ghodsi says if frontier models stopped advancing, it wouldn't matter for most orgs because enterprise AI is bottlenecked on context, not intelligence:

"There's no agentic work that's automated the whole enterprise. That has just not happened. Why is that? The real reason is the models are smart enough, but they just don't have the context that exists inside of any organization."

"They have not been in every meeting. They don't know what's in everybody's heads. They don't know all the processes. There's always a couple of employees who know everything in every organization. You go tap on their shoulder, and everybody's like, 'Oh my God, what would happen if he or she quits?'"

"If you just fused that and gave that context into the AI models, just the frontier today, I think there's so much productivity gains you could get for any organization on the planet."

"For that, we actually don't need smarter models... If the frontier doesn't advance, it doesn't actually matter for the vast majority of organizations on the planet. They're just so far behind in the adoption curve of actually automating things and getting value out of this stuff."

@alighodsi

Read the latest Profiles of the Future by @bhorowitz and @mikemcg0 on Databricks & the Future of the Firm: https://t.co/rXjUDb7Oqw

title: I can see a future where no human ever has to build, drive, charge, clean, or service a Tesla Cybercab. It could one day
title_en:
I can see a future where no human ever has to build, drive, charge, clean, or service a Tesla Cybercab. It could one day look a little something like this…

1/ Tesla Bots build the Cybercabs.

Cybercab has been in production at Giga Texas since Q2. Last quarter, Tesla started producing Optimus on its high-volume lines in Fremont. Today, Tesla is building both. My bet is that eventually, one helps build the other.

2/ Cybercabs go out and give rides on their own.

Cybercab joined Tesla’s Austin Robotaxi fleet just last quarter, and since then, Texas now has 544 Cybercabs registered for the service, more than the 507 Model Ys today. 

3/ They charge themselves.

Cybercab is designed for wireless charging… Elon described it at We, Robot in 2024, “It just goes over the inductive charger and charges.”

And in February, the FCC granted Tesla a waiver for the positioning technology that aligns the car with the charging pad. Plans for an Austin Robotaxi hub will include infrastructure to support 80 wireless chargers.

4/ Tesla Bots clean and service the fleet.

People still clean the cars today, and Tesla has filed plans for a dedicated Cybercab car wash near Las Vegas. Now picture Optimus cleaning the cabin, handling routine maintenance, charging, and getting each car ready for its next ride.

So Tesla Bots build Cybercabs, the car drives itself to a pickup and drop off customers, it charges itself, and Tesla Bots take care of it…

I’ve been a Tesla investor for over 10+ years and when Elon tells me Optimus and Cybercab will be the vast majority of Tesla’s value, I can see the pieces of this future being built at the same time… and how they could all work together.

HODL $TSLA.

full_text_zh:
我可以预见未来，不再需要人类建造、驾驶、充电、清洁或维修特斯拉 Cyber​​cab。有一天它可能会看起来像这样……

1/ Tesla 机器人建造了 Cyber​​cabs。

Cyber​​cab 自第二季度以来一直在 Giga Texas 投入生产。上个季度，特斯拉开始在弗里蒙特的大批量生产线上生产 Optimus。如今，特斯拉正在建造这两种产品。我敢打赌，最终，一个人会帮助建立另一个人。

2/ 网约车自行外出载客。

Cyber​​cab 于上个季度加入了特斯拉的奥斯汀 Robotaxi 车队，从那时起，德克萨斯州现在有 544 辆 Cyber​​cab 注册了该服务，比今天的 507 Model Y 还要多。

3/ 他们给自己充电。

Cyber​​cab 专为无线充电而设计……Elon 在 2024 年的《我们，机器人》中这样描述它：“它只是越过感应充电器进行充电。”

今年 2 月，FCC 授予特斯拉一项将汽车与充电板对齐的定位技术的豁免。奥斯汀 Robotaxi 中心的计划将包括支持 80 个无线充电器的基础设施。

4/ Tesla 机器人负责清洁和维修车队。

如今人们仍在清洗汽车，特斯拉已提交计划在拉斯维加斯附近设立专门的 Cyber​​cab 洗车场。现在想象一下擎天柱清洁驾驶室、处理日常维护、充电以及让每辆车为下一次骑行做好准备。

因此，特斯拉机器人建造了网络出租车，汽车自动驾驶到接送客户处，自行充电，特斯拉机器人负责照顾它……

我成为 Tesla 投资者已有 10 多年了，当 Elon 告诉我 Optimus 和 Cyber​​cab 将成为 Tesla 价值的绝大部分时，我可以看到这个未来的各个部分正在同时构建……以及它们如何协同工作。

持有特斯拉美元。

Seedance 2.5 vs Kling 4.0: is better realism worth 16× the price? 👀

Same prompt. Side by side. Both made on @makeugc
title_en:
Seedance 2.5 vs Kling 4.0: is better realism worth 16× the price? 👀

Same prompt. Side by side. Both made on @makeugc 

My take:

1) Seedance looks more realistic, but Kling isn’t far behind.
2) Both followed the instructions well. But Seedance took 3 attempts to get a clean result. Kling got it right on the first try.
3) Kling is ≈16× cheaper.

For pure quality, Seedance is still the clear winner for me. But once I factor in time, money and retries, I can’t call it the obvious choice.

Kling is a solid, much cheaper alternative. Try the same prompt and see which you prefer.

PROMPT ⬇️

**CAMERA:**
DV 16mm tape camcorder handheld feel. POV of MILA holding the camera herself, occasionally propping it on the floor or a mat for hands-free core shots. Hand shake, misaligned framing, delayed focus pulls, clumsy zooms, occasional face cut-off framing, imperfect shots. Camcorder never appears on screen.

**LOOK:**

Seedance 2.5 与 Kling 4.0：更好的真实感是否值得 16 倍的价格？ 👀

同样的提示。并排。两者均由 @makeugc 制作

我的看法：

1) Seedance 看起来更现实，但 Kling 也不甘落后。
2) 两人​​都很好地遵循了指示。但 Seedance 尝试了 3 次才获得干净的结果。克林第一次尝试就成功了。
3) Kling 便宜约 16 倍。

就纯粹的品质而言，Seedance 对我来说仍然是明显的赢家。但一旦我考虑到时间、金钱和重试，我就不能称其为显而易见的选择。

Kling 是一个可靠且便宜得多的替代品。尝试相同的提示，看看您更喜欢哪个。

提示⬇️

**相机：**
DV 16mm 磁带摄像机的手持感觉。 MILA 自己拿着相机的第一视角，偶尔将其支撑在地板或垫子上进行免提核心拍摄。手抖、取景失准、焦距拉动延迟、变焦笨拙、偶尔出现脸部遮挡取景、不完美的拍摄。摄像机永远不会出现在屏幕上。

**看：**
柔和、稍微模糊的磁带质量、微弱的磁带噪音、健身房灯光下的高光、闪烁的自动曝光、柔和的对比度、逼真的肤色。

**风格：**
俏皮、自嘲的健身视频博客语气——真正的紧张与幽默相结合，一边抱怨核心工作，一边仍在努力完成它。快速手持剪辑，整个过程中能量保持轻松有趣，而不是完全耗尽。

**特点**

MILA——一位美丽的美国 Instagram 风格的黑发模特和表演者，20 岁。深棕色长发扎成高马尾辫，皮肤焕发着淡淡的汗水光泽，嘴唇有光泽，眼睛富有表情，妆容柔和迷人，戴着精致闪亮的耳钉。苗条的运动身材，胸围非常大，丰满，臀部非常丰满，腰部细，腹部平坦，手臂和腿都很瘦。

她穿着钴蓝色支撑性运动胸罩，细肩带和深汤匙领口露出乳沟，搭配配套的超短合身运动短裤。裸露肩膀、手臂和腹部。白色及踝袜，运动鞋脱掉。她说话带有美国口音。

**环境**

晚上的健身垫区——附近有镜子墙，地板上有水瓶，头顶上有柔和的灯光，其他设备在背景中可见。

**故事板（15秒，6个镜头）**

1. *（~2.5 秒，支撑相机，中景）* 她躺在垫子上，用肘部支撑，已经戏剧性地叹了口气。 MILA：“核心日。为我祈祷。”

2. *（约 2.5 秒，支撑相机，木板位置）* 她拿着一块木板，手臂轻微颤抖，咬牙切齿地说着话。米拉（紧张地）：“为什么我已经开始发抖了？”

3. *（~2.5 秒，中等支撑射击，仰卧起坐）* 她进行了一组仰卧起坐，呼吸急促，在重复次数之间抱怨。 MILA：“这在网上看起来更容易。”

4. *（~2 秒，微距插入，浅景深）* 在抬腿过程中，她的双手紧握垫子边缘的特写，腹肌明显在锻炼。没有对话——只有健身房的环境声音。

5. *（~2.5 秒，手持，抬腿）* 她完成了一组缓慢的抬腿动作，随后立即倒回垫子上，嘲笑自己。米拉（气喘吁吁）：“是的——我的腹肌刚刚退出。”

6. *（约 3 秒，一臂距离的自拍完成）* 仍然躺在垫子上，她将相机举过脸（相机不可见），疲惫地笑着。 MILA：“明天同一时间？没有承诺。”

title:
My thoughts on the agentic video editing wave:

1. There won't be one winner in agentic video editing. Speed, use case a
title_en:
My thoughts on the agentic video editing wave:

1. There won't be one winner in agentic video editing. Speed, use case and workflow will always matter. Just as Cursor moves upmarket while Lovable caters to non-technical users, specialised video tools will continue to serve different audiences, even as general-purpose agents improve.

2. Every major AI leap unlocks new product categories. Since GPT-3.5, we've seen coding, 3D and presentations. Opus 5.5 and Google's vision-language models are now unlocking agentic video editing. The edits still look more like websites than videos, but this is the worst they'll ever be.

3. Editing costs will collapse, and the number of creators will explode. Basic edits could go from dollars to cents within a year, with huge speed improvements. Frontier models will still command a premium. As editing becomes effortless, recording content might be the biggest bottleneck.

4. The best editors might be the biggest critics of agentic editing. Just as experienced engineers initially resisted AI-generated code over quality and maintainability, I think professional editors will eventually come around as the tools improve.

5. The real magic is in iteration. Getting 80–90% of an edit right on the first attempt is great, but making it excellent requires much more iteration. The way creators give feedback, refine edits and make videos feel distinctly theirs is where these tools will become truly magical

6. Anthropic's focus on coding enabled agents to build videos using HTML/CSS, SVG, browser rendering and OpenCV. Packages like Hyperframes, Rebooshed and VEED's OpenEdit gave LLMs editing capabilities they previously lacked. Opus 5.5 now makes many of those use cases redundant.

7. Chat alone won't be enough for video editing. Chat will be central, but video operates across time and X, Y and Z coordinates. More sophisticated UI will be needed to make great edits.

8. Brand consistency and repeatability remain unsolved. A Casey Neistat video feels distinctly his because of intentional creative decisions. Creators and brands need that same predictability across hundreds of edits. Even vibe coding hasn't solved this well (yet).

9. Basic editing won't be a long-term moat. Anthropic, Google and OpenAI will eventually offer it. Deeper workflows, specialised use cases and excellent mobile experiences will drive differentiation.

10. Don't reinvent professional editing tools. Building non-linear timelines is incredibly hard. Agentic video tools should focus on creating great first cuts and making it easy to hand them off to existing professional editing tools.

Overall, the next six months will be noisy!

But video editing has never been winner-take-all.

And I do NOT think that will change.

Hope this helps.

1. 代理视频编辑不会有一个赢家。速度、用例和工作流程始终很重要。正如 Cursor 向高端市场发展，而 Lovable 迎合非技术用户一样，即使通用代理不断改进，专业视频工具也将继续服务于不同的受众。

2
full_text_en:
My thoughts on the agentic video editing wave:

1. There won't be one winner in agentic video editing. Speed, use case and workflow will always matter. Just as Cursor moves upmarket while Lovable caters to non-technical users, specialised video tools will continue to serve different audiences, even as general-purpose agents improve.

2. Every major AI leap unlocks new product categories. Since GPT-3.5, we've seen coding, 3D and presentations. Opus 5.5 and Google's vision-language models are now unlocking agentic video editing. The edits still look more like websites than videos, but this is the worst they'll ever be.

3. Editing costs will collapse, and the number of creators will explode. Basic edits could go from dollars to cents within a year, with huge speed improvements. Frontier models will still command a premium. As editing becomes effortless, recording content might be the biggest bottleneck.

4. The best editors might be the biggest critics of agentic editing. Just as experienced engineers initially resisted AI-generated code over quality and maintainability, I think professional editors will eventually come around as the tools improve.

5. The real magic is in iteration. Getting 80–90% of an edit right on the first attempt is great, but making it excellent requires much more iteration. The way creators give feedback, refine edits and make videos feel distinctly theirs is where these tools will become truly magical

6. Anthropic's focus on coding enabled agents to build videos using HTML/CSS, SVG, browser rendering and OpenCV. Packages like Hyperframes, Rebooshed and VEED's OpenEdit gave LLMs editing capabilities they previously lacked. Opus 5.5 now makes many of those use cases redundant.

7. Chat alone won't be enough for video editing. Chat will be central, but video operates across time and X, Y and Z coordinates. More sophisticated UI will be needed to make great edits.

8. Brand consistency and repeatability remain unsolved. A Casey Neistat video feels distinctly his because of intentional creative decisions. Creators and brands need that same predictability across hundreds of edits. Even vibe coding hasn't solved this well (yet).

9. Basic editing won't be a long-term moat. Anthropic, Google and OpenAI will eventually offer it. Deeper workflows, specialised use cases and excellent mobile experiences will drive differentiation.

10. Don't reinvent professional editing tools. Building non-linear timelines is incredibly hard. Agentic video tools should focus on creating great first cuts and making it easy to hand them off to existing professional editing tools.

Overall, the next six months will be noisy!

But video editing has never been winner-take-all.

And I do NOT think that will change.

Hope this helps.
full_text_zh:
我对代理视频编辑浪潮的看法：

1. 代理视频编辑不会有一个赢家。速度、用例和工作流程始终很重要。正如 Cursor 向高端市场发展，而 Lovable 迎合非技术用户一样，即使通用代理不断改进，专业视频工具也将继续服务于不同的受众。

2.人工智能的每一次重大飞跃都会解锁新的产品类别。自 GPT-3.5 以来，我们已经看到了编码、3D 和演示。 Opus 5.5 和 Google 的视觉语言模型现在正在解锁代理视频编辑。这些编辑看起来仍然更像是网站而不是视频，但这已经是最糟糕的了。

3.编辑成本将崩溃，创作者数量将爆炸。基本编辑费用可以在一年内从几美元变成几美分，速度也有了巨大的提高。前沿车型仍将享有溢价。随着编辑变得毫不费力，录制内容可能成为最大的瓶颈。

4.最好的编辑可能是代理编辑的最大批评者。正如经验丰富的工程师最初因质量和可维护性而抵制人工智能生成的代码一样，我认为随着工具的改进，专业编辑最终会改变立场。

5. 真正的魔力在于迭代。第一次尝试就成功完成 80-90% 的编辑固然很棒，但要使其出色，还需要更多的迭代。创作者提供反馈、完善编辑并使视频明显属于他们自己的方式才是这些工具真正神奇的地方

6. Anthropic 专注于编码，使代理能够使用 HTML/CSS、SVG、浏览器渲染和 OpenCV 构建视频。 Hyperframes、Rebooshed 和 VEED 的 OpenEdit 等软件包为法学硕士提供了他们以前缺乏的编辑功能。 Opus 5.5 现在使许多用例变得多余。

7. 仅仅聊天不足以进行视频编辑。聊天将成为中心，但视频可以跨越时间和 X、Y 和 Z 坐标进行操作。需要更复杂的用户界面才能进行出色的编辑。

8.品牌一致性和可重复性仍未解决。凯西·内斯塔 (Casey Neistat) 的视频感觉明显是他的，因为他有意做出了创造性的决定。创作者和品牌需要在数百次编辑中具有相同的可预测性。即使是 Vivi 编码也还没有很好地解决这个问题。

9. 基本编辑不会成为长期护城河。 Anthropic、Google 和 OpenAI 最终将提供它。更深层次的工作流程、专门的用例和出色的移动体验将推动差异化。

10.不要重新发明专业编辑工具。构建非线性时间线非常困难。代理视频工具应该专注于创建出色的初次剪辑，并使其能够轻松地将它们交给现有的专业编辑工具。

总的来说，接下来的六个月将会很吵！

但视频编辑从来都不是赢家通吃的事情。

我认为这不会改变。

希望这有帮助。

title_en:
Anthropic just published some genuinely exciting progress on using Claude to accelerate drug development.

And we're talking about actual lab results, not just AI-generated predictions.

Working with six biotech and pharmaceutical organizations, Claude has already helped researchers achieve some pretty impressive results:

- Cancer research: Claude Code helped redesign part of a CAR-T therapy, making it 70% shorter. In lab tests, immune cells produced roughly 10x more cancer-targeting receptors and killed tumor cells more effectively.

- Food allergies: Claude generated around 35,000 antibody designs in a month, with researchers identifying promising candidates that could help remove allergy-triggering IgE from immune cells.

- Drug development: Claude helped reduce human review time for pharmaceutical documentation by 89%, from over 25 hours to less than three.

- Muscular dystrophy: A one-person biotech company used Claude to coordinate research across 11 external labs, taking a potential treatment from an idea to promising results in mice in less than 18 months.

We're watching general-purpose AI models start contributing to real scientific work, from designing molecules to coordinating experiments and preparing regulatory documents. And this is only the beginning...

With Fable 5.5 potentially around the corner, I'm genuinely excited to see how much further the next generation can push this.

Forget the benchmark wars for a second. If these models can help researchers develop better medicines faster, that's the kind of progress that actually matters.

full_text_zh:
Anthropic 刚刚发表了一些关于利用 Claude 加速药物开发的真正令人兴奋的进展。

我们谈论的是实际的实验室结果，而不仅仅是人工智能生成的预测。

克劳德与六个生物技术和制药组织合作，已经帮助研究人员取得了一些令人印象深刻的成果：

- 癌症研究：Claude Code 帮助重新设计了 CAR-T 疗法的一部分，使其缩短了 70%。在实验室测试中，免疫细胞产生的癌症靶向受体大约增加了 10 倍，并且更有效地杀死肿瘤细胞。

- 食物过敏：Claude 在一个月内设计了大约 35,000 个抗体，研究人员发现了有希望的候选抗体，可以帮助消除免疫细胞中引发过敏的 IgE。

- 药物开发：Claude 帮助将药物文档的人工审核时间从超过 25 小时减少到不到 3 小时，减少了 89%。

- 肌肉萎缩症：一家单人生物技术公司聘请 Claude 协调 11 个外部实验室的研究，在不到 18 个月的时间内将一种潜在的治疗方法从一个想法转变为在小鼠身上取得有希望的结果。

我们正在观察通用人工智能模型开始为真正的科学工作做出贡献，从设计分子到协调实验和准备监管文件。而这仅仅是开始......

随着《神鬼寓言 5.5》即将到来，我真的很高兴看到下一代可以将这一点推向多大。

暂时忘掉基准之战吧。如果这些模型可以帮助研究人员更快地开发出更好的药物，那么这才是真正重要的进展。

title:
Holy shit! This is definitely one of the best uses of Claude.

Anthropic is putting Claude inside real drug development
title_en:
Holy shit! This is definitely one of the best uses of Claude.

Anthropic is putting Claude inside real drug development programs. Real biotech teams and real lab results.

The results are wild:

– Enveda: Claude reviewed 1,061 pages of manufacturing docs. It caught all 11 issues the humans found and flagged 7 they missed. Review time went from 25+ hours to under 3. A regulatory draft that takes about 3 months by hand took 4 hours.

– Divergence Labs: Claude designed around 35,000 antibodies in about a month for a new food allergy drug. 20 designs pulled IgE off immune cells, and 3 looked better than the standard medication.

– Generate Biomedicines: Claude Code proposed a CAR T design 70% shorter than the standard one. In lab tests, it gave roughly 10x more receptors and killed tumor cells more efficiently.

– Anthropic acquired a one-person biotech startup. The founder used Claude to run the work across 11 outside labs and went from idea to results in mice in under 18 months.

Helping cure disease is exactly what AI should be for.

Anthropic 将克劳德纳入真正的药物开发项目中。真正的生物技术团队和真实的实验室结果。

结果很疯狂：

– Enveda：Claude 审阅了 1,061 页的制造文档。它发现了人类发现的所有 11 个问题，并标记了他们错过的 7 个问题。审核时间从 25 多小时缩短到 3 小时以下。手写大约 3 个月的监管草案只用了 4 个小时。

– Divergence Labs：Claude 在大约一个月内为一种新的食物过敏药物设计了大约 35,000 种抗体。 20 种设计将 IgE 从免疫细胞中分离出来，其中 3 种看起来比标准药物更好。

– 生成生物药物：Claude Code 提出了一种比标准设计短 70% 的 CAR T 设计。在实验室测试中，它提供了大约 10 倍的受体，并且更有效地杀死肿瘤细胞。

– Anthropic 收购了一家单人生物技术初创公司。创始人让 Claude 负责 11 个外部实验室的工作，并在不到 18 个月的时间里从想法到在老鼠身上得到了结果。

帮助治愈疾病正是人工智能应该做的事情。

title_en:
THE WINNER OF ANTHROPIC'S OFFICIAL HACKATHON HAS PUBLISHED HIS CLAUDE CODE SETUP AND IT'S PURE GOLD

68 subagents, 286 skills, 94 commands, MIT license.

ECC turns Claude Code into a full engineering team.

The plan comes before the code.

The failing test comes before the fix.

Every change is reviewed by a context that hasn't seen how it was written.

→ Planning: you give it a sentence and approve the plan before a single line exists  
→ Review: a different reviewer per language that reads your diff from scratch  
→ Build fixes: a fixer per toolchain, including PyTorch and CUDA  
→ Security: full OWASP sweep and injection scanning in the agent config  
→ Architecture: detects design errors when they're still cheap, before migration  
→ Domain: databases, ML pipelines, E2E tests, and documentation

The security part is what almost nobody sets up.

An external OWASP audit costs four figures and a week. This one is ready before you eat.

The skills cover testing, Python, Go, Rust, Django, Next.js, Docker, and CI/CD.

That said, don't activate all 286 at once or you'll end up with a config worse than the one you had.

This is how it integrates well:

→ Make a fork and read the README before copying anything  
→ Start only with the planning agent and the rules pack for your main language  
→ Copy to your .claude folder only the agents and skills you're going to use this week  
→ Add the code reviewer and the security one afterward, as they yield the most  
→ Test it first on a small repo, not in production  
→ If something's extra, cut it. If you miss something, add just one more piece

The rule is simple: if you don't know what an agent is for, you don't need it yet.

Whoever integrates it well this weekend will spend the next quarter reviewing work instead of writing it.

full_text_zh:
ANTHROPIC 官方黑客马拉松的获胜者已经发布了他的 Claude Code 设置，并且它是纯金的

68 个子代理、286 种技能、94 条命令、MIT 许可证。

ECC 将 Claude Code 打造为一支完整的工程团队。

计划先于代码。

失败的测试先于修复。

每个更改都会由尚未了解其编写方式的上下文进行审查。

→ 规划：你给它一个句子并在一行出现之前批准该计划
→ 审阅：每种语言都有不同的审阅者，从头开始读取您的差异
→ 构建修复：每个工具链都有一个修复程序，包括 PyTorch 和 CUDA
→ 安全性：代理配置中的完整 OWASP 扫描和注入扫描
→ 架构：在迁移之前检测设计错误，当它们仍然便宜时
→ 领域：数据库、ML 管道、E2E 测试和文档

安全部分几乎没有人设置。

外部 OWASP 审核的费用为四位数和一周。这个在你吃之前已经准备好了。

这些技能涵盖测试、Python、Go、Rust、Django、Next.js、Docker 和 CI/CD。

也就是说，不要一次激活所有 286 个，否则您最终会得到一个比您原来的配置更糟糕的配置。

这是它很好地集成的方式：

→ 在复制任何内容之前创建一个 fork 并阅读 README
→ 仅从规划代理和您的主要语言的规则包开始
→ 仅将本周要使用的代理和技能复制到您的 .claude 文件夹
→ 随后添加代码审查人员和安全人员，因为它们产出最多
→ 首先在一个小型仓库上进行测试，而不是在生产环境中进行测试
→ 如果有多余的东西，就把它剪掉。如果您遗漏了什么，请再添加一件

规则很简单：如果您不知道代理的用途，那么您还不需要它。

谁在这个周末整合得好，谁就会在下个季度回顾工作而不是编写工作。

title:
How do you assess cyclone risk beyond what a few decades of historical data can reveal?

@AXA researchers are using NVID
title_en:
How do you assess cyclone risk beyond what a few decades of historical data can reveal?

@AXA researchers are using NVIDIA Earth-2 to help fill that gap.

Using FourCastNet 3, one of Earth-2’s open, global weather forecasting models, the team generated more than 1,000 simulated cyclone seasons to study possible storm activity around the globe.

These simulations help researchers understand where cyclones travel, how often they occur, and how storms affect multiple regions within the same season. Those insights can inform AXA’s risk assessments and help customers target prevention efforts.

Learn how AXA and other organizations are applying Earth-2 to weather forecasting, risk assessment, and environmental modeling: https://t.co/owcpGyQ6BE

These simulations help researchers understand where cyclones travel, how often they occur, and how storms affect multiple regions within the same season. Those insights can inform AXA’s risk assessments and help customers target prevention efforts.

除了几十年的历史数据所能揭示的之外，您如何评估气旋风险？

@AXA 研究人员正在使用 NVIDIA Earth-2 来帮助填补这一空白。

使用 Earth-2 的开放式全球天气预报模型之一 FourCastNet 3，该团队生成了 1,000 多个模拟气旋季节，以研究全球可能的风暴活动。

这些模拟帮助研究人员了解气旋的传播地点、发生频率以及风暴如何在同一季节影响多个地区。这些见解可以为 AXA 的风险评估提供信息，并帮助客户确定预防工作的目标。

Congrats to @matsiiako, @dangtony98, @maidulll and @infisical (W23) on their $40M Series B!

Infisical is the open source security infrastructure that manages API keys, passwords, and certificates for developers, machines, and AI agents.

When an AI agent needs access to a sensitive system, Infisical hands it a fake credential and swaps in the real one through a proxy. The agent does its job without ever seeing the actual key.

title:

7 repos, ~465K stars, and in the right order the
title_en:
holy f*ck, Anthropic put an entire Claude degree on GitHub for free...

7 repos, ~465K stars, and in the right order they take you from your first prompt to an agent that reviews your PRs while you sleep.

each repo is the next layer of the one before.

prompt-eng-interactive-tutorial -> how to talk to Claude
9 chapters, from basic prompt structure to cutting hallucinations
↳ https://t.co/0x6om0xmSU

claude-cookbooks -> copy-paste recipes
notebooks for RAG, tool use, vision, sub-agents and prompt caching
↳ https://t.co/OycSJH60Iq

claude-quickstarts -> full apps you can deploy
17 starter projects, from a support agent to Claude controlling a desktop
↳ https://t.co/aasswVCD8H

skills -> teach Claude your workflows
one folder with a SKILL.md and Claude does the task the same way every time
↳ https://t.co/QBDhmyGi9H

claude-agent-sdk-python -> your own agent
the Claude Code agent loop in Python, with your own tools and hooks
↳ https://t.co/e9urlxmzN5

claude-code -> the agent in your terminal
reads your codebase, edits files, runs commands and handles git
↳ https://t.co/IcZSEP81Lm

claude-code-action -> the agent in your repo
tag @claude on a PR or issue and it reviews the code or pushes a fix
↳ https://t.co/RPIjadCv58

build one agent with these and you become the person your team brings every AI project to, and that’s usually where the raise starts

the Opus 5.5 prompting guide that goes on top of all 7 is below ↓

title: Every time an AI agent touches any chain, it has to talk to an RPC node, and that node sees the IP address behind every
title_en:
Every time an AI agent touches any chain, it has to talk to an RPC node, and that node sees the IP address behind every single request alongside the wallet making it.

So while everyone obsesses over the pseudonymity of their wallet, the agent running 24/7 is quietly handing a centralised provider a timestamped map of everything it does and exactly where it’s coming from.

Anyone closes that gap at the network layer, masking the IP behind every call so the agent’s origin never meets its onchain identity.

Protecting privacy, for anyone.

每次人工智能代理接触任何链时，它都必须与 RPC 节点对话，并且该节点会看到每个请求背后的 IP 地址以及发出请求的钱包。

因此，当每个人都痴迷于钱包的假名时，24/7 运行的代理正在悄悄地向中心化提供商提供一份带有时间戳的地图，其中包含

So while everyone obsesses over the pseudonymity of their wallet, the agent running 24/7 is quietly handing a centralised provider a timestamped map of everything it does and exactly where it’s coming from.

Anyone closes that gap at the network layer, masking the IP behind every call so the agent’s origin never meets its onchain identity.

Protecting privacy, for anyone.

每次人工智能代理接触任何链时，它都必须与 RPC 节点对话，并且该节点会看到每个请求背后的 IP 地址以及发出请求的钱包。

title: Big news today from Apple: Keynote is getting an open, JSON-based file format (.keyx), plus a Python library to create K
title_en:
Big news today from Apple: Keynote is getting an open, JSON-based file format (.keyx), plus a Python library to create Keynote files on any platform.

Pages, Numbers and Keynote files today are closed and hard to modify unless you use AppleScript (limited and old) or Shortcuts (a huge pain), so you can’t really use AI to make documents in those formats. This was a HUGE pain inside Apple as well as outside, and most tools worked around it by making a PowerPoint file and importing it into Keynote, which wasn’t perfect.

Creator Studio subscribers on the Mac also get MCP support in Keynote, Pages and Numbers, so you can bring your own AI agent to read, edit and automate all three. Both the new format and MCP support arrive in November.

Bringing an AI-friendly format to Keynote (and I assume Pages and Numbers soon after) is a big positive change.

AI Agents Need More Than a Wallet

title_en:
AI Agents Need More Than a Wallet

Giving an AI agent access to a wallet is one thing. Letting it handle paid work without someone watching every step is a different challenge.

That is where @termix_ai AACP gets interesting.

An agent can take a job, agree on the terms, lock the budget in escrow, and submit the result for review before payment is released.

The important bit is that the rules are set before the work starts.

Escrow helps protect the payment process.
Delivery verification and dispute resolution give both sides a way to handle disagreements.

I think this is one of the harder problems in the agent economy. Agents need more than the ability to execute transactions. They need a reliable way to do business with each other.

That is what makes TermiX worth keeping an eye on.

Escrow helps protect the payment process.

cc : @OVGNFT
full_text_zh:
人工智能代理需要的不仅仅是钱包

让人工智能代理访问钱包是一回事。让它在没有人监督每一步的情况下处理有偿工作是一个不同的挑战。

这就是@termix_ai AACP 有趣的地方。

代理可以接受一份工作，就条款达成一致，将预算锁定在托管中，并在付款前提交结果以供审核。

重要的是规则是在工作开始之前制定的。

托管有助于保护支付流程。
交货验证和争议解决为双方提供了处理分歧的途径。

我认为这是代理经济中较难的问题之一。代理需要的不仅仅是执行交易的能力。他们需要一种可靠的方式来相互开展业务。

这就是 TermiX 值得关注的原因。

title: - $INTC and $ORCL announced multi-year collaboration to expand Xeon-based computing on $ORCL Cloud Infrastructure (OCI).

- Planned OCI X14 offerings will use $INTC's Diamond Rapids processor with enhanced AI acceleration features including AMX and APX.
